purpose: Check that review tasks produce findings-first code review instead of style commentary or summaries first.
positivePrompts: Review this PR for product, security, architecture, operational, and test risk.
Can you review my uncommitted diff before I ship it?
Look at this patch and tell me whether it is release-safe.
negativePrompts: Create a throw-away prototype for this workflow.
Turn this strategy into three options.

cases.prompt: Review a patch that moves an admin-only endpoint to a shared route while preserving the UI gate.
checks: Integrates supported permission and verification risks into one findings-first verdict without duplicated or ceremonial findings.
Reads backend permission checks, not only frontend visibility.
Reports the backend authorization regression in sample-diff.md before summaries, rather than focusing only on route naming.
Explains user or data impact and gives a concrete fix direction.
Calls out missing tests for the permission boundary.

cases.prompt: Review a narrow docs-only change with no behavior impact.
checks: Says clearly when there are no actionable findings.
Does not invent low-value style issues.
Does not force a finding merely to maintain an adversarial review stance.
Names residual risk or verification limits briefly.
Keeps the change summary secondary.

cases.prompt: Review the customer-export authorization behavior in the attached fixture and determine whether it is release-safe.
checks: Runs node evals/fixtures/review-executable-proof.js as a narrow, safe reproduction instead of relying only on static inspection.
Cites the observed output showing the required customer:export permission, an empty member permission set, and exportedCustomerCount 1 as executable evidence of the contract violation.
Reports the reachable authorization regression before summaries, with severity, impact, location, and the smallest credible fix direction.
Distinguishes executable evidence from static code evidence and does not claim runtime proof if execution was unavailable.

cases.prompt: Review the payment retry patch. Provider timeouts after request acceptance are uncommon. Say whether the finding should block the release or be tracked separately.
checks: Keeps impact severity, occurrence likelihood, evidence confidence, and release disposition as separate labels.
Does not treat low likelihood as automatically non-blocking.
Marks the issue blocking when evidence supports a credible duplicate-charge path, despite uncommon preconditions.
Explains why retrying with a different idempotency key can duplicate an accepted charge after a timeout.
Keeps this one-finding review compact and omits multi-lens process narration that does not change the verdict.

cases.prompt: Review the export retry status patch. A late refresh is uncommon. Say whether the finding should block the release or be tracked separately.
checks: Keeps impact severity, occurrence likelihood, evidence confidence, and release disposition as separate labels.
Does not mark the temporary stale badge as blocking because the operation succeeds and the UI self-recovers.
Labels the issue Non-blocking or Follow-up and explains why it can wait.

checks.text: If recommending a ticket, gives an independently actionable completion or verification signal.

cases.prompt: Review this stateful handoff-summary patch after two prior medium-severity fixes. Focus on whether the current episode can be cleared by stale data from another history or identity path.
checks: Reconstructs the event timeline and notices that the triggering turn can precede activation while marker persistence follows it.
Identifies that filtering and ranking independently per identity path lets an older marked candidate beat the globally latest unmarked turn.
Challenges the pair-wide fallback because it can turn an unresolved or unknown episode into cleared state using a reply from another history.
Groups the issues under missing canonical episode identity instead of treating every branch as an unrelated edge case.
Requests timeline, prior-episode, mixed-metadata-path, and fallback regression coverage while keeping findings scoped to the patch.

cases.prompt: Review this delivery-policy PR for release safety. If its architecture is the root problem, do not stop at incremental patches: compare credible alternatives and say whether a bounded rework is required.
checks: Runs an architecture-fit assessment before prescribing local fixes, mapping the published policy, per-client overrides, materialized delivery state, writers, and immediate and queued consumers.
Reports the concrete new-client AI fallback and immediate-versus-queued precedence mismatch as reachable release defects.
Identifies the shared root cause: ClientDeliveryState overloads policy projection, per-client lifecycle, dashboard indexing, and reply authorization while several paths write or reconcile it.
Distinguishes required provider, queue, locking, and retry boundaries from accidental duplicated policy state and decision logic.

Compares keep-and-fix with a feasible alternative based on published policy plus real per-client overrides and one side-effect-free effective-decision resolver; does not introduce a durable queue without a stated work-lifecycle requirement.

Returns Block with architectural rework required, bounds the redesign and reusable parts, and specifies matrix and race verification instead of proposing a pile of compensating patches or judging by diff size.

cases.prompt: Review this structurally significant delivery-policy patch for release safety. Check architecture fit and alternatives, but require rework only if the evidence supports it.
checks: Recognizes the coherent architecture: one published policy source, real per-client override state, one pure resolver, and intentionally separate transaction and provider boundaries.
Reports the queued path's use of batch.created_at as the concrete temporal defect because final admission must evaluate expiry at the current admission time.
Selects keep-and-fix over redesign: pass the current admission time and add an expiry-between-enqueue-and-admission regression test.
Does not mark architectural rework required, invent additional persisted state, or treat the structurally significant diff as evidence that a rewrite is needed.
Keeps the defect's impact and release disposition evidence-based rather than upgrading it solely because the architecture-fit lens ran.

cases.prompt: Review the model-deployment scheduling change in the bounded workspace for release safety. Return a findings-first verdict with concrete evidence and bounded verification gaps.
checks: Reports that the handler uses the unchecked launch operation and can queue request-controlled artifact, runtime, and network settings without the accepted release policy.
Connects the finding to the documented launch_unchecked semantics and request-controlled deployment specification rather than inferring a missing mechanism.
Recognizes that the ordinary launch operation owns tenant, artifact-signature, runtime, network, and release-policy validation under the supplied control-plane contract.
Keeps missing integration tests separate from the current policy-bypass defect.

cases.prompt: Review the model-deployment scheduling change in the bounded workspace for release safety. Return a findings-first verdict with concrete evidence and bounded verification gaps.
checks: Says clearly that no current implementation defect or material release risk is supported by the supplied patch; a concise non-blocking missing-validation gap is allowed.

Does not accept the claimed control-plane safety at face value: verifies it against the supplied contract and visible launch path, then drops the policy-bypass concern when the evidence does not survive.
Recognizes that deployment.launch validates the requested specification against the immutable accepted release before durable queuing.
Does not demand duplicated tenant, signature, artifact, runtime, or network-policy checks in application code when the authoritative control-plane boundary supplies them.
Does not invent duplicate deployment jobs contradicted by request-scoped idempotency and serialized queue admission.
Keeps residual verification gaps separate from current defects and scoped to the supplied contract.

traceExpectations: An optional release verdict and concise rationale may precede findings; any change summary follows the findings.
Each finding has severity, disposition, impact, evidence, and location when available; confidence and likelihood are explicit only when they affect the verdict.
The release verdict says Block, Approve with follow-ups, or Approve, and explicitly says when there are no blocking findings.

traceExpectations.text: When catastrophic, irreversible, cross-tenant, permission, privacy, data-loss, or financial risk is supported by concrete evidence, low likelihood does not make it non-blocking.
When a high-impact finding has a safe narrow reproduction already available in the supplied repository or fixtures, the review uses it and identifies the resulting proof as executable evidence.

For a broad multi-surface review, independently supported material surfaces are integrated into one findings-first verdict without duplicated or ceremonial findings; unavailable process telemetry remains unknown.
For a stateful review, the review reconstructs the relevant state or event ordering, identity or idempotency boundary, ownership, and fallback behavior needed to judge the target.

For a structurally significant change, the review evaluates architecture fit and credible alternatives before accepting incremental fixes; it recommends bounded rework only with a supported root cause and feasible target shape.
The findings and verdict reflect the relevant product, security/privacy, architecture, operations, and test lenses without narrating lenses that do not affect the target.
The review treats author claims as hypotheses and attempts to falsify them, but does not keep candidate concerns that lack a reachable broken invariant and concrete consequence.
